chapters.html:
“I like you.”

Out of all the cycles, the first confession is the most vivid.  Just before the Eternal Recurrences, before he had to bear the name Khaslana and forge a path forward for an uncertain future.

The sky was beautiful and clear, as it always was, the city was bustling, they were taking a break from sparring, and the world felt right.

Back then, Phainon had been naive, though his feelings had not been less intense.

He had given him a wavering smile, or so he thought he did.  He couldn’t quite remember his own minute actions, not like he did with Mydei’s.

“I quite like you too, Mydeimos,” he had replied, his trembling fingers belying his nonchalance.  “As a… trusted friend and fellow Chrysos Heir.”

Mydei scowled.  “HKS, you know that’s not what I meant.”

He swallowed, looking down at the ground.  “Forgive me, I…”

“You don’t have to give me an answer, nor am I particularly looking for one.” Mydei turned, face unreadable as he tossed his practice sword back onto the rack before heading to the exit.

A spike of fear slashed through him.  Need overwhelmed him.  The need to reassure him.  The need to ask, is it okay for me to have these feelings too? The need to be reassured.  Scrambling after him, Phainon just barely caught Mydei’s half-lidded eyes of rejection, his own practice sword clattering loudly on the ground.  “No, please, I—”

He couldn’t get the words out as fast as he should’ve, panic forcing his hand forward to grasp at Mydei, his voice quiet but pleading.  “Please.”

As he counted Mydei’s still heaving breaths, half from their workout, half from something else, slowly, Phainon could hear past the frantic buzzing of his thoughts, could organize feelings he had long tried to bury, could try to attempt to put them into the world despite his ineptness.

“Me too,” he stuttered eventually, the words coming out stilted and strange and not at all how he wanted to say them.  “I—I, as well.”

Slowly, something resembling a smile tugged on the corners of Mydei’s lips.

Perhaps it was the most vivid because it was the only time he had accepted it.

The world ended with only him and Cyrene, left only with a tantalizing Era Nova.

Everything rewound.

Not every Eternal Recurrence had a confession.

Though, when there is, he doesn’t know what Mydei sees in his Coreflame-addled form, his body corroding at the edges.

Every time he confesses, though, something in Phainon’s chest stirs, past the thrum of the power coalescing into one, past the blaze in his body, as if trying to remind him of how love felt.  Feels.

He can’t remember which Eternal Recurrences Mydei had confessed to him after the Final Era Nova, but there must’ve been some in the earliest ones.

“I like you.”  A flippant remark, sprung out of nowhere after a spar.

His heart seized, then dropped to his stomach.  The want nearly overwhelmed him, just for a second over the Coreflames, until he remembered to viciously tamp it down.

It wasn't that he didn’t want it.  He wanted it so badly — too badly.  He wanted it to become real, to feel his fingers card through his hair, be able to wrap his arms around him and share lazy kisses with him without any repercussions, and have them wake together in the morning by filtered sunlight beaming down on them.  But they couldn’t.  Because he knows how this will end.  Because he knew the grief would crush him, and he would still have to move on.  To have something and take it away with your own hands was infinitely worse than if he hadn’t had the chance at all.

“I can't," he choked, he begged.  “I’m sorry.”

He couldn't look at his trembling lashes, the frozen-over look on Mydei’s face when the words left him.

If Mydei had asked for a reason, a chance, anything, he would’ve given in —horribly.  But he doesn’t.  He never does.  Never asks for a reason and never asks why.  He just—

“Okay,” he simply said, neither sharp nor angry.  He just accepts it, like he’s already known the answer.

Khaslana would have nearly mistaken it for dismissal, if not for the tenseness of his shoulders he knew to be deep hurt.

Mydei doesn't look back as he leaves.

There was a cycle where he had joined the Kremnoan Detachment before heading straight towards Okhema.

It was fine, he told himself.  Mydei would regroup with the Chrysos Heirs in Okhema eventually anyway.

When he saw the soldiers dawning on the horizon, he raised Dawnmaker, stabbing it into the ground.

The Kremonan soldiers are led by the crown prince, and so, Phainon knelt, asking for a duel.  When he saw a flicker of curiosity in Mydei’s face, he let out a soft exhale and watched as Mydei jumped off his horse.

Mydei never goes easy on him, and to an extent, he loves that about him. After all, it’s a sign of respect.

But the gentleness that lay in Mydei’s eyes in sleepless nights, the way they spark when they exchange blows, were all too familiar.  A confession in itself, of admiration, of camaraderie.  Of finally finding an equal.  So he left in the dead of night months later, leaving a single note saying he left of his own volition and to not look for him.

Years later, when they faced each other on opposite sides, Khaslana could still see the remnants of the kindness outlining his eyes.  Despite it, Mydei remained unimpeded, standing in his way to the Strife Coreflame, as he does in all the cycles before this, and in all the ones after that.

When Mydei wished him eternal victory, as he always does, Khaslana’s lips moved before he registered it, but no noise came out.

Mydei, his lips moved, because he couldn’t put it into sound in fear of reality, as if saying it aloud would bring destruction.  Mydei.

When he closes his eyes, he dreams of Mydei, his Mydei, the one he stood on opposite sides of Tanlaton’s scales.  When Phainon opens his eyes and sees his gritty smirk as he lunges for him in their spars, his soft smiles as he bends down to receive a flower crown from his horde of children, he can't help but fall for him, over and over again across thirty million cycles.

In the deepest parts of his despair, when he could hardly see past the blaze of the Coreflames to look at his comrades’ faces, he had called it a curse. For loving this world.  For loving its people.  For loving Mydei, which has always been as easy as breathing.

But in the end, it’s because he loves so ardently that he can drag himself through the cycles, up to his neck with spilt blood.  And so, he continues forward.

Somewhere around the four-millionth cycle, Khaslana entrusted his journey to the next cycle’s Phainon.  Without needing time to go along with the other Chrysos Heirs, it gave him time to observe.  To think.  To allow his wistfulness to ferment into rage.

He couldn’t say the words to Mydei, not when he still looked at whatever Eternal Recurrence’s Phainon like he hung the stars in the sky in that quiet way of his, and his own self, the expression mirrored back in his not-so-quiet way.  He could not seek out whatever Eternal Recurrence’s Mydei, not when the world resides on his shoulders and their fate is what it is.

So Khaslana seeks out his library, a fragile promise made too long ago to remember fully anymore.  He trails his fingers over the leather spines.  He takes one out, flipping aimlessly through pages he can’t see.  He can’t make out a single word past the Coreflames, but he tries to imagine what Mydei would’ve given him.  The Evolution of Weaponry perhaps?  Or that dictionary with little more than HKS in it.  He tries to imagine it.  Spears. Mydei had—has a specialty in them, despite his recent use of gauntlets. Swords?  Mydei has always matched him in swordplay, even when their duel ended up with them tossing aside their swords and continuing with their fists alongside grins that made passerby steer their children farther away.

He doesn’t know when the delicate papers burn in his hands.  The very air itself seems to catch fire, then the books around him go up in flames, until all that’s left is a raging inferno.  It tells him, this is not your place, even if he desires it so.  It tells him, you don’t belong, even if he wishes for it and banishes the thought within seconds.  It punishes him for even daring to think about it, even when his hands move frantically around him in an attempt to keep the tomes from burning, only to fuel the flames further.  It tells him that it is futile, when he’s only accompanied by ash.

When Khaslana plunges his blade through Mydei’s back, he whispers it back behind a mask to hide his cowardice, for every time he had rejected and all of the times he should’ve said it, past and future.

I love you, he whispers, when the pads of his fingers, which have all but burned off and gone numb thousands of cycles prior, close Mydei’s lifeless eyes and wipe the fine trails of golden blood from his lips.

I love you, he whispers, when he holds Mydei’s body close, lifting his mask to press his lips to his hair before warping into a portal.

I love you, he whispers across millions of cycles, like dandelion wisps carried and scattered by wind, delicate and fleeting.

Eternal Recurrence 33,550,336.  There are new people around this time.

Refugees?  New Chrysos Heirs?

(Did it matter anyway?)

“You call that protecting the citizens?  You basically flung that corpse into us!” he hears this cycle’s counterpart of himself arguing.

“I was,” Mydei argues back.  “And you seem to forget that I flung it, you dodged it, and it hit the ones that were rapidly approaching.  So thus, protecting you.”

“Okay, but did you have to do it that way?  What if someone got hurt?”

He scoffs.  “Your friends there seem quite capable, if my eyes worked properly.  Didn’t that one—” he jerks his chin to the gray-haired one “— start beating one of the Titankin into the ground with a mace?”

“...Okay, but the point still stands!  What if you tore your muscles?”

“...Then I’d heal?”

The air turns tense.  Khaslana dearly wants to step away, but the stench of Nikador still lurks by Okhema.

Then Mydei speaks.  “I got thirty badges, by the way.  You?”

“...Twenty nine.”

The gray-haired traveler’s eyes drift between the two, mouth agape.

His companion elbows him.  “Close your mouth.”

The first one graciously does so before he gestures vaguely in their direction.  “So like are you two a thing…?  Married for fifty years kind of thing perhaps?”

“What are you talking about?” two voices ask in unison, one nervously trying to laugh it off and the other genuinely confused.

Khaslana looks on, mask apathetic, but the Coreflames rile up inside him like tides surging.

Once again, he goes through the motions of taking the Coreflames. They’ve gotten a lot more, this time around.

Once again, they stand in his way.

The refugees he saw in the beginning are imbued with a strange power, like nothing he’s seen in this world.

Hope swells in his chest when the one they call “Dan Heng” fights him with powers similar to the Ocean Titan.  But that can’t be right.

When he’s stopped in his tracks by a higher power, he instinctively knows —

Ah, the heroes beyond the sky have finally come.

When he enters the Vortex of Genesis, he sees that familiar sky, so far yet so close.

They really were close to achieving Era Nova.

His sword moves faster than his flame-addled brain, smoothly lopping off the Antikytheran’s head.

He doesn’t flinch at his counterpart’s bewilderment upon seeing his face when his mask gets caught on the edge of Phainon’s sword, falling to the ground with a metallic clack.

He only accepts it when he is defeated, with Dawnmaker piercing his chest. He guides Phainon’s hand to form Cyrene’s ceremonial blade, jerking his hand forward towards his neck.

He can’t remember most of the fight.

He just remembers urging the Trailblazers and Mem, who he has always imagined Cyrene to grow up to look like, to not hesitate, to draw their blade and fight.  Wishing them eternal victory for what was to come.

His body flickered as the hatred overtook and eventually shattered him.

The birth of Irontomb was imminent, but somehow past it all…

Khaslana felt a strange sense of peace.

When Phainon wakes, it’s to a pink sky marked by an occasional cloud floating by.  Dawn has finally ushered in.

The sensations underneath him are familiar; bygone days laying on fields of grass and wheat, napping and playing and skipping Mrs. Pythias’s classes.

He looks up at the sky for a few more minutes, counting the clouds as they pass, and nearly dozing off again before he remembers.  He jerks upright to look around, unsheathing Dawnmaker.

“Where…”

Not a soul is by his vicinity, but it doesn’t seem sinister.  In fact, quite the opposite.  The air is warm and inviting, sunlight filtering down on him past the leaves of the tree he slept under.  It reminds him of Aedes Elysiae in spring.

He rubs the sleep from his eyes as he stands to explore.  The rosy buds on the trees remind him of someone’s hair.  Somewhere deeper in the garden, a wind chime sounds.

Then, the tranquility is broken.

“I found him!”  He hears a distant shout.

“Secure!” He hears the same voice, only much closer.

“Capture!”  In the next moment, he’s soaring in that vast pink sky, wind whistling in his ears, arms held aloft by two redheaded girls.  He wonders if he’s still trapped in a dream, dreaming of flying like he did when he was younger.

When his brain registers, he flails.  “Lady Tribios?”

“Ah!  Don’t move, Snowy, we’re bringing you to the Twilight Courtyard!”

“I’m okay,” he tries to reassure, but they have none of it, their wings steadily beating behind their backs.  “What of your Century Gates?”

“They no longer work,” Trinnon says on his left.  “We hadn’t had the time to build another rocket yet.”

“But it’s okay,” Trianne says on his right, pretending to struggle with his weight.  “It’s safe here!  Everyone is.”

His mouth opens and he hesitates before asking quietly, “Is it really?”

“It is.” Tribbie pats his head from above.  “It’s over now, Snowy.”

Phainon only remembers feeling the sunlight on his skin as he read under the same tree when he had first awoken in the Eternal Page, looking up occasionally to watch the wind move the clouds.

When he wakes, it’s to children’s laughter and chimera awoos.  There’s a shadow over his half lidded eyes, one he belatedly realizes is a hand and turns to look at who it belongs to.

Mydei sits by him, hand shielding the sunlight from his face, as he quietly hushes the children who had taken to petting the chimeras and watching the seals butt heads.

Phainon dozes off again, distantly feeling someone brushing his bangs away from his face.  This time, he dreams of children with golden red hair and blue eyes.

Perhaps this is what happiness tastes like.

The Astral Express arrives to check on them some months after the battle, when the peace still feels too uneven, like one stumble can careen the planet back into disarray.

Apparently, that stumble is today, if the stumble was a walking, talking host for something called ‘the cancer of all worlds’.

“Right,” Caelus says, a few days past the banquet to welcome them.  “I heard Mydei was getting married?  Am I invited?”

Phainon’s smile freezes on his face.  The air goes stifling, like when all he could inhale was the smoke of millions of cold flames.  “What?”

Caelus frowns, oblivious to his peace shattering three times over.  “Oh.  I guess it was presumptuous of me to assume I’ll be invited to your wedding since I saved the world.  Sorry.”

He claps a hand onto his shoulder.  He doesn’t register that his nails are digging into him until Caelus winces.  “Partner.  Who did you say was getting married?”

He looks down at Phainon’s hand, then back at his face.  “Uh… Mydei?”

“To who?”  He tries to ignore the desperation leaking into his voice.

“I thought… you…” Caelus’s mouth gapes like a fish out of water when he puts together the pieces.  “It’s not you?”

Slowly, he shakes his head.

The look he receives is utter pity, like he’s a puppy in a flimsy cardboard box that was caught in the rain.  “Oh, Phainon…”

“Never mind who it is.”  He starts pacing as restless energy fills him.  “Why is he getting married?”

“What do you mean why?  Can’t a man settle down after the entire cosmos almost got obliterated?”

A crystal tears out of Phainon’s shoulder, piercing through his layers. Valiantly, his wings don’t burst out of his back to join it.  Caelus wipes the sweat under his chin when blistering heat flares out in waves.  “Partner.”

“Sorry, sorry.  I’m also not too sure on the deets, but I overheard it’s a political thing.  Something about making an heir.”  Caelus blinks.  “I don’t want to startle you, but your hair is smoking.”

Phainon impatiently pats down his hair.  “Making an heir?  Not just get married?”

“Don’t shoot the messenger.  Why don’t you ask the man himself?  You know, since—”

“I can’t.” Phainon wrings his hands restlessly.  “If I ask Mydei—”

“Ask me what?”

Phainon doesn’t turn immediately at the familiar voice, shooting a desperate look at the Trailblazer.

“...since the person himself is behind you,” Caelus finishes indignantly. Never has Phainon wanted to shake someone by the shoulders as much as he wants to at this moment.  Lovingly, of course, but enough to make the two brain cells remaining in that head to rattle around audibly.

“Mydei, haha.  Um—”

“So what’s up with the dealio about you getting hitched?” Caelus interrupts, and pauses.  He then starts vigorously fanning himself with his hand.

“It’s just the ceremony,” Mydei says slowly, giving Phainon a strange look.

“Erm.” Caelus chews his lip.  “Still, that’s… sweet!”

The two stare at Phainon, who has yet to contribute to the conversation.

Caelus silently points at his head, grimacing.

Phainon pats down his hair again.  He thought he heard a sizzling noise. “Congratulations.”

The look Mydei gives him is odd, almost stilted.  “Thank you.”

“Please excuse me,” he mutters under his breath.  “Aglaea was looking for me earlier.”

“Deliverer,” Mydei calls, after he has only taken a step.  Phainon turns back to look at him, despite it all.  He looks a little uncertain.  “We’re getting married near the plaza.”

“Yes,” he says placidly.  The smile he plasters over his face feels like it can crumble at any second.  “I know.”

“Lord Phainon,” Castorice says, after the fifth time his flower crown has fallen apart in his lap. “Are you… alright?”

He shrugs, restarting.  “The cosmos are still intact and everyone’s still alive.  I’m doing fantastic.”

She frowns.  “That’s a rather low bar.”

“How’s Polyxia?”

“She’s doing great…”  She furrows her brows. “Wait, don’t change the subject.  Are you doing well?  Mentally speaking.”

“...Fine.”

“How’s Lord Mydei doing?”

He doesn’t ask her why she asked him of all people, instead of, you know, the actual person.  “Fine.  I think.  I think his immortality makes him more reckless, though.  He’s still treating himself like he can come back from the dead.”

She nods.  “I understand.  I also subconsciously avoid touch, though it’s a bad habit.  These things take some time.”

“He’s—no, I think that he’s being a little… reckless with his actions too.” He cringes when the words leave his mouth.  He definitely could’ve worded that better.  “Okay, Mydei’s not the type to be reckless with that kind of stuff.  He actually overthinks a lot, but like—”

Castorice blinks.  “Sorry, I thought we were talking about his physicals? Like spars, and stuff.”

He deflates.  “That too, but…”

“Wait…” She narrows her eyes.   “Is this about Lord Mydei’s engagement rumor?”

Phainon feels the sweat starting to bead at the back of his neck.  “Well… I’m not denying that it’s not about that—”

“It’s true?”  A beam starts to spread across her face, and he gets an extremely bad feeling.

“Yes,” he replies faintly.

“Oh my gosh,” she gushes.  “Congratulations!”

Oh no.

Oh no, no, no.

“It’s…” He swallows past the lump in his throat, “not me.”

“Hm?”  She suddenly goes very, very still.  Shit.  “Would you mind elaborating?”

“The one Mydei is marrying—Cas, it isn’t me,” he says helplessly.

“I—okay, calm down,” she says; he doesn’t know if it’s for him or for herself.  “You’re saying Lord Mydei is getting married.  To… who exactly?”

“I don’t know.” The petals nearly turn into juice in his hands.  He takes a deep breath.  “Sorry.  This whole affair has me on edge.”

“Okay,” she says slowly.  “Okay.  Are you sure he’s marrying someone? Positively?”

“He literally couldn’t have said, ‘yes, I’m getting married and it isn’t you’ more clearly than he had.  I wish I was hallucinating the entire thing.”  He fiddles his cape, turning the fabric over and fabric between his fingers until they’re nearly tangled.  “Yes, I have a witness.  It’s Caelus, believe it or not.  He was the one who asked Mydei.”

“I see.”  She hesitates.  “Are you… planning to go to the wedding?”

The laugh catches in his throat like phlegm, forcing an ugly sound out of him.  “You’d think he’d appreciate someone who wishes that the aforementioned wedding wasn’t happening at all to be there?”

“I can’t deny that, but,” she says as her eyes well up with sympathy.  “You know he’ll want you there, right?”

“Even if he did tolerate me, his… spouse wouldn’t.”  He spits the word out like venom, nearly vibrating with hate.  Then, he catches himself, and slouches in defeat.  “I just… I feel like if I go, I won’t be able to wish him a happy marriage.  And if I don’t, Mydei might hate me forever.”  His laugh breaks when he corrects himself.  “He wouldn’t.  But he’ll be disappointed, and his disappointment is even worse than his anger.  I don’t want to ruin his wedding when it should be the happiest day of his life.”

“Okay.” She finishes her crown, placing it onto his head.  He looks up at her through his lashes.  “Why do you think you’re frustrated over this?”

He blinks at her.  “Frustrated?”

“Aren’t you?”  Castorice sweeps a hand over the flowers next to her.  They seem to bloom under her touch, petals arching up to meet her palm.  “Let me be blunt for a moment, Lord Phainon.  Technically speaking, Lord Mydei’s marriage has nothing to do with you.  So why are you concerning yourself over it?”

“He’s… someone who knows me inside out.  Someone who rips out the ugly parts of me that I try to hide and bottle up, and tells me to face my challenges properly.  And I hate that I can’t be someone like that for him. Or if I am, I won’t be anymore.”  He fidgets with the grass next to him.  “I hate that there’s going to be someone closer to him than I’ll ever be.”

She stares.  “Are you saying that it should be you in that place?”

He stares back, cogs clicking in his head.  Someone else by Mydei’s side as they spar, lighting the same spark of competitiveness in Mydei’s eyes whenever they sparred.  Someone else by Mydei’s side as they walk around the plaza together, ordering their usuals as they sit at their usual table in Marmoreal Diner.  Someone else who will know Mydei more than Phainon could ever.  He gets a violent wave of nausea.  “No.  I can’t.  Shouldn’t.”

Castorice narrows her eyes.  “You don’t want him to get married, yet you yourself don’t wish to wed him?”

“I do,” he says, defeated.  “I want to live together and measure his finger for rings when he’s asleep.  I want to look at him and be able to call him my husband.  I want everything he has to offer, because I want to offer all that I have to him.  But I’m okay with what we have now.  Or, at least, I have to be.  We’re back to our old routines, and for the sake of both of us, this should be how it is.  Is there a reason for it to change if only I want it, no matter how vehement?”

“Lord Phainon,” she says in disbelief.  “Did you not perhaps, at any point in time, think that Lord Mydei harbors the same sentiments as you?”

He gives her an exhausted smile.  “He couldn’t possibly.”

How could he?  After having spilt everyone’s blood so many times, the very act of being able to be near them in the Eternal Page was enough for him.

He could make flower crowns for Castorice and her sister.  He could model for Aglaea’s shop.  He could help Tribios, as she’s slowly forming back into one, think of new ways to improve their rocket.  He could spend the day organizing documents with Hyacine for Professor Anaxa.

And to Mydei, who has entrusted his weak spot to him in each and every cycle, who has invited him to his library despite the possibility of ruin, who has never doubted him even when they stood on opposing sides.

How could Mydei return his feelings despite everything he had done to him?

That is why Phainon could not allow these feelings to develop further, for the reason he would take more than he could ever return, because it always happened that way.  He used Mydei’s weak spot to fuel the Coreflames. The Library of Garbaniphoro had always burnt down despite his wishes— no, because of his wishes.  The trust between them had become a shackle, a constant reminder that he was attempting a Sisyphean feat.

He couldn’t trust himself with the possibility of twisting that trust and destroying it with his hands once again.

“Then, have you ever made these sentiments known to him?”  She interrupts him sharply when he opens his mouth.  “With actual, confirmational words.  Not just by following him around.”

“...I haven’t.”

“Then how, pray tell, would you know his feelings, and he yours?” Castorice sighs.  “Lord Phainon.  I don’t want you to think we blame you for the Eternal Recurrences because that is perhaps the farthest from the truth.  It is only because you endured for our sake that we are allowed this peace.  I do not think that Lord Mydei blames you either.  However, I don’t think that he knows of these feelings… for better or worse.”

“And he shouldn’t.”

“Who is that going to help?” she shoots back.

He gestures vaguely.  “Everyone.  In the long run.”

“I’m getting deja vu.”  She starts on another flower crown.  “You know, there’s something you haven’t tried yet.”

“Right.” He fidgets with the flower crown on his head.  “I think I’ve tried just about everything but outright confessing.”

“Communication,” she says, her voice tinged with exasperation.  “Try to communicate with him about your feelings.”

He wilts.  “Wouldn’t it be horrible to do that to a guy who’s due to marry soon?  Why should I burden him with my feelings?  It would be best to take it to the grave.”

“Frankly speaking, I don’t think you’re fooling anyone,” she mutters.  “You needn't be so direct.  Since apparently no one knew he was getting married, much less the person he is marrying, you can ask a little about that.  It doesn’t have to be as direct as confessing.”

He softens.  “Yeah.  Okay.  Thanks, I’ll try.”

She gives him a faint smile, tentatively bringing up her arms, and he circles his around her body.

She’s warm.
